Get the dimensions of a Swiss Stats Explorer dataset

Source: R/bfs_sse.R
bfs_sse_dimensions.Rd

Get the dimensions of a dataset of the Swiss Stats Explorer (SSE) API (https://stats.swiss/) and the values allowed in each dimension. Use them to build the filters of bfs_sse_data().

Usage

bfs_sse_dimensions(dataset, ..., language = "de", version = NULL)

Arguments

dataset

The id of a dataset, e.g. "DF_LWZ_1": the column dataset of bfs_sse_datasets(), also shown in the URL of the dataset on https://stats.swiss/.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty: the arguments after dataset must be named. The arguments of bfs_get_sse_metadata(), such as number_bfs, give an error that names their new name.

language

Language of the labels: "de" (default), "fr", "it" or "en". A label missing in this language falls back to another language.

version

Version of the dataset, e.g. "1.1.0": the column version of bfs_sse_datasets(). If NULL (default), the API uses the latest version. Set it in a data pipeline to keep the same structure when a new version is published.

Value

A tibble with one row per value allowed in each dimension (some values may have no data):

dimension

The dimension id, to use as a name in filters.

dimension_label

The dimension label.

value

The value code, to use as a value in filters.

value_label

The value label.

position

The position of the dimension in the dataset.

parent

The code of the parent value in the codelist, e.g. the district of a commune and the canton of a district, or NA. Use it to select all the values under a value.

Returns NULL if there is no internet connection.

See also

bfs_sse_datasets(), bfs_sse_data()

Author

Felix Luginbuhl

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
dimensions <- bfs_sse_dimensions("DF_PASTA_552_MONTHLY", language = "en")
dimensions

# the dimensions only
unique(dimensions[c("dimension", "dimension_label")])

# the communes of the canton of Geneva: the values whose parent is a
# district of Geneva
regions <- bfs_sse_dimensions("DF_LWZ_1", language = "en")
districts <- regions$value[regions$parent %in% "GE"]
regions[regions$parent %in% districts, ]
}
